simple.meaning: בְּעָא (bᵉʻâʼ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to seek or ask.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 12 times across Daniel, beginning at Daniel 2:13. Its contexts include Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בְּעָא (H1156).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: בְּעָא (bᵉʻâʼ) / H1156 is traced through Daniel 2:13, Daniel 2:16, Daniel 2:18, Daniel 2:23 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: So the decree went out, and the wise men were to be slain. They sought Daniel and his companions to be slain.
Daniel went in, and desired of the king that he would appoint him a time, and he would show the king the interpretation.
that they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret; that Daniel and his companions would not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
I thank you, and praise you,
Daniel requested of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the affairs of the province of Babylon; but Daniel was in the king’s gate.

This was fulfilled the same hour on Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven from men, and ate grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky, until his hair had grown like eagles’ feathers, and his nails like birds’ claws.
Then these men said, “We won’t find any occasion against this Daniel, unless we find it against him concerning the law of his God.”
Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it not be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn’t alter.”

Then they came near, and spoke before the king concerning the king’s decree: “Haven’t you signed a decree that every man who makes a petition to any god or man within thirty days, except to you, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions?”

Then they answered and said before the king, “That Daniel, who is of the children of the captivity of Judah, doesn’t respect you, O king, nor the decree that you have signed, but makes his petition three times a day.”
Then the king, when he heard these words, was very displeased, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him; and he labored until the going down of the sun to rescue him.
I came near to one of those who stood by, and asked him the truth concerning all this.

definitions.full: H1156. bea בְּעָא verb ask, seek , only Daniel (Biblical Hebrew בעה (rare)); — Pe`al Perfect 3masculine singular ׳ב Dan 2:16 , 49 ; 3 masculine plural בְּעוֺ 2:13 ; 1 plural בְּעֵ֫ינָא 2:23 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יִבְעֵא 6:8 ; 6:13 ; 1 singular אֶבְעֵאֿ 7:16 ; Infinitive לְמִבְעֵא 2:18 ; Participle בָּעֵא 6:12 ; 6:14 , plural בָּעַ֫יִן 6:5 ; — 1 ask, request , with מִן person Dan 2:16 (object clause with דִּי ), 2:49 ; 7:16 (+ accusative of thing); ask of God 2:23 (+ id. ), of God or man 6:8 (+ accusative of congnate meaning with verb), 6:13 ; with מִןקֳֿדָם of God 2:18 (accusative of thing); = pray , ׳ב א ׳וּמִתְחַנֵּקֳדָם 6:12 , ׳ב 6:14 . 2 seek , accusative of person Dan 2:13 , accusative of thing 6:5 .
